findings.claim: c2/measure.py docstring lines 12-13 and 17: 'only the self-test was measured, so env-diff --contract (the one other documented mode that allocates scratch) was outside the contract'; 'grammar 8 allocating modes (the seven self-tests + env-diff --contract)'. Contract target: 8/8 allocating modes.
findings.fact: registry-check run --rev is a documented mode (usage + docstring + SKILL.md:2180) that allocates at tools/registry-check.py:780 via clone_lane_at_rev; the documented allocating population is 9, not 8.
findings.impact: With TMPDIR set-but-unusable the mode exits 2 but prints 'REGISTRY_CHECK: could-not-evaluate (...)' on stdout, stderr empty: no frozen-grammar line. A complete 9-mode counter would read grammar=6/9 at base, and could not be 8/8 without editing registry-check.py (not in the round's integration list). As frozen, C2_R55_PASS=true is reachable while a documented allocating mode violates the class.
findings.pinned_shape: The tool's own selftest --rev cases (registry-check.py:1640-1646) record rev-unknown with check_lines(proc, ['REGISTRY_CHECK: could-not-evaluate']) -- the paren/stdout shape is asserted by the selftest, so aligning --rev with the frozen grammar would require changing that assertion as well. The counter's grammar arm runs only --selftest, which reaches strict_scratch_root at :930 before the --rev cases block, so the mode is never observed.

findings.claim: Round-55 note says 'Eight allocating modes carry it' (worktree corpus/knowledge/scratch-root-contract.md:77) and 'the round-55 counter measures every documented allocating mode' (:66-67); the registry cell registry-check-selftest says 'Allocating modes: selftest.'
findings.fact: The honest count is nine; registry-check's cell must say 'selftest, --rev' and the note must name registry-check --rev. The note's own blind-spot paragraph locates the hole 'outside the registry and the usage text'; this hole is inside both the usage text and SKILL.md:2180.
findings.impact: Adding the ninth name does not break the frozen counter: the note arm counts only that its eight labels appear, and the docs arm only needs the MARKER substring, so the docs can be made true without touching frozen files.

findings.severity: boundary note (not a defect under the frozen surface)
findings.claim: bash-witness-study run/rerun are documented modes that can cause scratch to be created under $TMPDIR.
findings.fact: They do not call strict_scratch_root; they shell out to tools/mutate-and-run.sh, whose mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/tameshi-r4-2-run.XXXXXX" (tools/mutate-and-run.sh:491) is a child allocation. At base the runner-drift precondition stops both before the sweep (r11c/r11d), so this is code-read only.
findings.impact: A bad TMPDIR there yields the runner's SETUP message, not the frozen grammar; the counter's surface ('the seven tools that call strict_scratch_root()') excludes it, so this is recorded, not scored.
